provenance: Priority 2 round-3 held-out T3 set, authored 2026-10-20 before any round-3 measurement on it. It replaces the round-2 set (seed 20261021), whose baseline saturated at 20/20 and therefore had no headroom to prove a gain; that set is retained only as saturation evidence. Modules here were drawn by random.Random(20261022) from 606 impl files that have a sibling .test.ts(x), are >1500 bytes, and lie outside every directory of the development set and both earlier held-out sets; the first 10 sampled were used without replacement. Required paths are the module, its test, and one import-adjacent collaborator whose role the task describes without naming it, except two scenarios where the module has no relative collaborator. Authoring bias: the author knew the relations under test (binding references, overflow-aware traversal) while writing; collaborators are import-adjacent by construction, which favors structural relations. No target is given for any task. Pre-registered gate rule: the gate is met only if, on this set, a variant or the binding baseline beats both the old-database baseline and its same-database baseline by at least 2 net selected required paths with at least one newly passing scenario, zero errors, and zero false-complete outcomes.

scenarios.task: Find the workspace file preview that distinguishes an inaccessible workspace from an inaccessible file while preserving error messages from older servers, and keeps a comment annotation attached to its lines when the underlying viewer remaps an anchor line. Include the annotation range logic it relies on and the tests.

Explain how remote shell connections ask for passwords: the recognized prompt shapes, the helper descriptor used to ask outside the terminal, and the error type that carries failures back to the caller. Include the tests.
Find the loader that reads project files for the server, including the typed load failure it raises when a file cannot be used, and its tests.

Find the mobile cache that shrinks oversized project icon encodings, deletes its temporary thumbnail files, releases a decoded image when its request was canceled, and rejects an image the native decoder did not actually downsize. Include the mobile database it attaches to and the tests.

Review the desktop main window: it leaves fullscreen before concealing a pending quit, restores saved bounds only when they fit a connected display, and recognizes only same-origin renderer navigations. Include the window wrapper it builds on and the tests.
Find the broker that serves preview automation invocations for the server's tool surface, including the invocation context it threads through each call, and its tests.

Explain how the server decides what kind of machine it runs on: marketing names and model identifiers on one platform, firmware virtualization markers preferred over chassis type on another, without mistaking one vendor's physical hardware for a virtual machine. Include the command runner it probes through and the tests.

Find the proxy that fetches remote content for HTML previews while never reaching this machine or its local networks, including translated and tunneled address forms that would otherwise smuggle a local address past the check. Include its tests.

Find the desktop pool that registers and reuses backend instances under stable identities, refusing a duplicate registration, together with the per-instance manager it delegates lifecycle to. Include the tests.

Find one hosted source-control provider integration: how it discovers repositories and serves pull-request operations by driving the vendor command-line tool it wraps. Include the wrapper and the tests.
